title: Removing one top-dimensional nondegenerate simplex
statement:
Let $A$ be a simplicial set with finitely many nondegenerate simplices, in the conventions of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Let $d\geq0$ and assume every nondegenerate simplex of $A$ has dimension at most $d$. Choose a nondegenerate simplex $\sigma\in A_d$. For each $m\geq0$ define
$$U_m=A_m\setminus\{A(\alpha)(\sigma)\mid\alpha:[m]\twoheadrightarrow[d]\text{ is order preserving}\}.$$
Then the $U_m$, with the operators restricted from $A$, form a simplicial subset $U\subseteq A$. Under this inclusion the nondegenerate simplices of $U$ are exactly the nondegenerate simplices of $A$ other than $\sigma$. In particular $U$ has finitely many nondegenerate simplices, all of dimension at most $d$, and one fewer nondegenerate $d$-simplex than $A$. Moreover $U_m=A_m$ for $m<d$, $A_d=U_d\amalg\{\sigma\}$, and every simplex of $A_m\setminus U_m$ for $m>d$ is degenerate in $A$. The case $d=0$ and the possibility $U=\varnothing$ are included.

proof.text: Let $t\in U_m$ and $\theta:[r]\to[m]$. Suppose $A(\theta)(t)=A(\alpha)(\sigma)$ for a surjection $\alpha:[r]\twoheadrightarrow[d]$. By the cited decomposition write $t=A(\beta)(y)$ with $\beta:[m]\twoheadrightarrow[e]$ and $y$ nondegenerate; the hypothesis gives $e\leq d$. Enumerate the image of $\beta\theta$ in increasing order to factor it as $[r]\xrightarrow{q}[k]\xrightarrow{i}[e]$, with $q$ surjective and $i$ injective, so $k\leq e$. Decompose $A(i)(y)=A(\gamma)(z)$ with $\gamma:[k]\twoheadrightarrow[\ell]$ and $z$ nondegenerate. Functoriality gives $A(\theta)(t)=A(\gamma q)(z)$. Since $\gamma q$ is surjective, uniqueness against $A(\alpha)(\sigma)$ implies $\ell=d$ and $z=\sigma$. Thus $d=\ell\leq k\leq e\leq d$, so $\ell=k=e=d$. An injective or surjective increasing self-map of a finite ordinal is the identity, hence $i=\gamma=\mathrm{id}$ and $y=z=\sigma$. Consequently $t=A(\beta)(\sigma)$ was removed, contradicting $t\in U_m$. All operators therefore preserve the $U_m$, which form a simplicial subset by the cited definition. The image enumeration and the finite-ordinal inequalities are elementary finite-order arguments.

source.place: Stacks Tag 018S (lemma-add-simplices), proof: choose a maximal nondegenerate simplex and read the adjoining construction in reverse; the deletion formulation is agent-written.

proof.text: An ambient nondegenerate $m$-simplex in the removed set has the form $A(\alpha)(\sigma)$ with $\alpha:[m]\twoheadrightarrow[d]$. If $m>d$ this is degenerate by definition, and if $m=d$ then $\alpha=\mathrm{id}$. Thus the only removed ambient nondegenerate simplex is $\sigma$. Every other ambient nondegenerate simplex lies in $U$ and remains nondegenerate there, since a degeneracy expression in $U$ would also be one in $A$. For the converse take $t\in U_m$ nondegenerate in $U$ and use the cited decomposition to write $t=A(\beta)(y)$ with $\beta:[m]\twoheadrightarrow[e]$, $y$ nondegenerate in $A$, and $e\leq m$. Define $s:[e]\to[m]$ by choosing the least element of each fiber of $\beta$; these least elements increase, and $\beta s=\mathrm{id}$. Step 1 gives $y=A(s)(t)\in U_e$. If $e<m$, the expression $t=U(\beta)(y)$ makes $t$ degenerate in $U$, a contradiction. Hence $e=m$, $\beta=\mathrm{id}$, and $t=y$ is nondegenerate in $A$. This proves exactly the claimed identification.

proof.text: The preceding identification makes the nondegenerate simplex set of U a subset of the finite nondegenerate simplex set of A with exactly σ deleted. Hence U has finitely many nondegenerate simplices, all have dimension at most d, and the number of nondegenerate d-simplices drops by one.

source.place: Stacks Tag 018S (lemma-add-simplices), conclusion after deleting one maximal nondegenerate simplex.

proof.text: For m<d there is no order-preserving surjection [m]↠[d], so U_m=A_m. In degree d the only surjection [d]↠[d] is the identity, so A_d=U_d⨿{σ}. If m>d, every removed simplex is A(α)(σ) for a nonidentity surjection α:[m]↠[d], and is therefore degenerate in A. These observations include d=0 and the case U=∅.

lean.statement: theorem finite_simplicial_top_simplex_removal (A : SSet.{u}) [A.Finite] (d : ℕ) [A.HasDimensionLE d] (σ : A _⦋d⦌) (hσ : σ ∈ A.nonDegenerate d) : ∃ (U : A.Subcomplex), (∀ (m : ℕ) (x : A _⦋m⦌), x ∈ Set.range (U.ι.app (op ⦋m⦌)) ↔ ∀ (α : ⦋m⦌ ⟶ ⦋d⦌) [Epi α], A.map α.op σ ≠ x) ∧ (∀ (m : ℕ) (y : (U : SSet).nonDegenerate m), y.1.1 ∈ A.nonDegenerate m) ∧ (∀ (m : ℕ) (y : (U : SSet).nonDegenerate m), ¬(m = d ∧ HEq y.1.1 σ)) ∧ (∀ (m : ℕ) (x : A _⦋m⦌), x ∈ A.nonDegenerate m → (m = d ∧ HEq x σ ∨ ∃ y : (U : SSet).nonDegenerate m, y.1.1 = x)) ∧ (∀ (m : ℕ), m < d → Set.range (U.ι.app (op ⦋m⦌)) = Set.univ) ∧ (∀ (x : A _⦋d⦌), x ∈ Set.range (U.ι.app (op ⦋d⦌)) ↔ x ≠ σ) ∧ (SSet.Finite (U : SSet)) ∧ (SSet.HasDimensionLE (U : SSet) d) ∧ (∀ (m : ℕ) (x : A _⦋m⦌), d < m → x ∉ Set.range (U.ι.app (op ⦋m⦌)) → x ∈ A.degenerate m)
